Avodah Zarah 6a:14.english: A dilemma was raised before the Sages: Is the reason for the prohibition against conducting business with gentiles in the days preceding their festivals because the gentile might profit, which will bring him joy, and he will subsequently give thanks to his object of idol worship on his festival? Or perhaps it is because this is a violation of the prohibition: “And you shall not put a stumbling block before the blind” (Leviticus 19:14), as one who sells an animal to a gentile thereby aids him in engaging in prohibited idol worship.

Avodah Zarah 6a:5.english: A dilemma was raised before the Sages: When the mishna teaches that it is prohibited to conduct business with gentiles on the three days before their festival, do the three days include the days preceding the festival and the festival itself, in which case the prohibition applies only to the festival and the two preceding days? Or perhaps the Gemara's question is that it is referring to the three days preceding the festival, without including the festival itself, which are certainly prohibited in and of themselves.
